The repair replaces that pre-trap nextTick claim with one @opened lifecycle handler — no timers, no retries, no trap disabling — that claims row focus only while the dialog is still open and the trap still holds its container default, never overriding a deliberate user focus move to the columns input or a footer button, and preserves everything else: opening defaults 4×3, declared limits rows 1–30 / columns 1–20, reset on reopen, Cancel creating nothing, exactly one createTable dispatch with the user-entered dimensions and dialog close. A new tests/e2e/table-dialog.spec.ts proves the production renderer through the actual menu-command/dialog path in chromium and webkit-tables: default 4×3 opening with stable row focus, Cancel creating nothing, and real 7×5 input confirmation producing exactly one matching table — real DOM rows/cells plus canonical Markdown. Verification bookkeeping refreshes M-011/V-M-011 records and local semantic markup; no other runtime, dialog design, dependency or infrastructure file is in scope.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: src/renderer/src/components/editorWithTabs/editor.vue replaces the nextTick(() => rowInput.value.focus()) claim inside handleEditParagraph with the exact lifecycle repair pinned in the implementation notes: the el-dialog template gains @opened="handleDialogTableOpened"; handleEditParagraph keeps only the 4×3 tableChecker reset and dialogTableVisible = true; the new handleDialogTableOpened claims row focus only while dialogTableVisible is still true AND document.activeElement is still the focus trap's container default (null/body, the .ag-dialog-table dialog container or the .el-overlay), then calls rowInput.value?.focus(). No setTimeout/setInterval/rAF retry, no trap disabling, no synthetic focus stub, no focus assertion removal; the trap's containment and close-time focus restoration are untouched; the nextTick import stays for its other call sites.
